significance.root_decision: For all s >= 2 and n >= 2, M_s(n+1) <= M_s(n) + 1, where M_s(n) is the least positive c such that every spanning subgraph G of the complete multipartite graph with c classes of s vertices either contains a 4-cycle or leaves some vertex with at least n non-neighbours in other classes (a star K_{1,n} in the complement relative to the host). This is Conjecture 2.3 of Goncalves, Monte Carmelo and Nakaoka, who proved the inequality only under an additional numerical hypothesis by keeping the original partition. The proof here proves the stronger step that the property at (n, c) implies the property at (n+1, c+1) by abandoning the partition: delete s suitable vertices and re-partition the rest into c independent s-sets, by a one-vertex swap forced by C4-freeness when s >= 3, and for s = 2 by a friendship-type lemma (two vertices with no common neighbour) with a perfect matching in the complement, plus explicit small cases. Lean defines the host graph, the property and the minimum literally, and proves that the minimum exists.
significance.caveat: Prior art not fully cleared: three texts by the same authors could not be read by any lane (their 2020 paper in Brazilian Journal of Development, their 2021 paper in Procedia Computer Science 195, and the first author's 2019 thesis; the sites refuse automated clients). The abstracts that could be read mention no such step bound; the cross-model reviewer puts 'not public' at 0.85. Read them before publishing. The MathDB record says 's-partite'; the source means c classes of s vertices each, which is what Lean states. The proof is short (about fifteen lines of idea) and elementary; the cross-model reviewer rates it not routine at 0.6 and overall about 0.5. No second cross-model lane read the finished Lean: root compared the definitions and the theorem with the endpoint that reviewer had written and found them identical.
